status: Parameter normalization verified; full native rendering remains unimplemented

findings: Picture Controls apply to RAW and merged pixel-shift images.
Camera compatible and Latest Picture Control select distinct color reproduction behavior.
Latest Picture Control permits newer controls on RAW images from older camera models.
Flexible Color requires SDR and the latest Picture Control processing path or a camera with that path fixed as Camera compatible.
Advanced controls include sharpening at three spatial ranges, contrast, highlights, shadows, white level, black level and saturation.
Custom tone curves replace direct contrast, highlights, shadows, white-level and black-level adjustment.
Color Blender adjusts hue, chroma and brightness for eight color regions.
Color Grading adjusts hue, chroma and brightness for highlights, mid-tones and shadows, with shared blending and balance.
Only cameras supporting Flexible Color can import Flexible Color custom controls; these controls cannot be adjusted on the camera.
Custom Picture Control exchange formats are NCP, NP2 and NP3.
Format compatibility varies by camera; NP3 support alone does not establish Flexible Color support.
Exported camera files use NIKON/CUSTOMPC; import/export also supports ordinary files.
NX Studio can store up to 150 custom controls; that application limit is not a proven file-format limit.

Constructor RVA0x28d200 sets default grid32; setup RVA0x28d3d0 copies0xdc8 configuration bytes and applies requested_grid|1, giving33 for request32. Preparation RVA0x2ae7b0 allocates three uint16 channel planes, invokes table generation, then overwrites table bytes0..71 with nine RGB-to-XYZ doubles selected by engine+0x9c0. It also reads NKDBase_NEF.icm. The direct scalar probe reconstructs the required context but does not exercise the application lifecycle.

scalar_mode_oracle.status: Historical probe superseded by scalar_matrix_oracle below
scalar_mode_oracle.input: Neutral family12 state, camera1071, grid32, generated table from0x29f0b0, input indices16/16/16.
